Single-Prediction Collapsed Agent Model

Single-prediction collapsed Bayesian agent model.

This is a further reduction of agent_model.MultivariateAgentModel for the case where the agent observes a single scalar prediction pred_o for a single observed feature vector X_o. Under independent Gaussian priors, the coefficient vectors N_b and N_d and the population means alpha_mu_A and alpha_mu_Y are marginalized analytically. The sign of N_E is also summed out: NUTS samples only U = abs(N_E), while both signed branches are evaluated in the likelihood.

The reduced-plate auxiliary variables (s, W, g, h) of the multivariate model are replaced by two scalar auxiliaries (R, T), constant in both the plate size n and the number of covariates k. Conditional on \(U=|N_E|\), R, T, the remaining scale parameters, and X_o, the observed prediction follows an exact two-component Gaussian mixture. For sign \(s\in\{-1,+1\}\), the branch mean is

\(M_s=m_Y+su\,m_A+x^\top(m_b+su\,m_d)\),

and its variance is

\(W_s=v_Y+u^2v_A+\sum_jx_j^2(v_{b,j}+u^2v_{d,j}) +(u^2\alpha_{A_\sigma}^2+\alpha_{Y_\sigma}^2)(1/n+R/T)\).

The mixture weights retain both branches of the normal prior on N_E, so no independence between sign and magnitude is assumed. The coefficient-prior cross term is absent because this class assumes independent N_b and N_d. The auxiliary R has the exact law

\(n R \sim \chi'^2_k(\lambda)\), \(\lambda = n \Delta_X^2\),

with \(\Delta_X^2 := (X^o - \vec{\alpha}_{X\mu})^\top D_X^{-2} (X^o - \vec{\alpha}_{X\mu})\). For \(k > 1\), R is drawn from the native non-central chi-squared in distributions. For \(k = 1\), the equivalent signed Cochran construction is used instead:

\(R = (\delta_X + G_R / \sqrt{n})^2\),

where \(\delta_X = (X^o - \alpha_{X\mu}) / \alpha_{X\sigma}\) and \(G_R \sim \mathcal{N}(0, 1)\). Thus \(nR = (\sqrt{n}\delta_X + G_R)^2\) has exactly the required \(\chi'^2_1(n\delta_X^2)\) law while avoiding direct sampling at the singular boundary of a one-degree-of-freedom chi-squared distribution. The number of sampled plate primitives remains two (G_R and T for k = 1; the non-central chi-squared and T for k > 1), independent of k and n.

The signed N_E, alpha_mu_A, alpha_mu_Y, N_b, and N_d are reconstructed jointly after sampling. Once the sign is drawn, their conditional distribution is Gaussian, so Matheron’s rule gives exact draws for predictive summaries and do(A) outcomes. CATE moments are Rao–Blackwellized over both signs.

class single_prediction_collapsed_agent_model.SinglePredictionCollapsedAgentModel(n_covariates, plate_size, prior_parameters=None)[source]

Bases: object

Bayesian agent model for the single-prediction collapsed likelihood.

The class assumes independent Gaussian priors for N_b, N_d, alpha_mu_A, and alpha_mu_Y. These quantities and the sign of N_E are marginalized analytically. PyMC samples the magnitude of N_E, the remaining population parameters, and the two scalar auxiliaries (R, T).

The model always assumes an OLS predictive model with intercept, and is specific to a single observed prediction: it does not extend, in this form, to more than one prediction. Because the CATE depends only on N_E, the prior and posterior CATE are obtained from signed N_E. The marginalized variables are recovered jointly from their exact conditional posterior for predictive summaries and expected-outcome helpers.

Parameters:

  • n_covariates (int) – Number of covariates k (dimension of X).

  • plate_size (int) – Size of the plate (number of i.i.d. samples used to train the predictive model). Must be larger than n_covariates.

  • prior_parameters (dict) – Dictionary with parameters for the prior distributions. If None, defaults are used. Vector-valued entries accept a scalar (broadcast to length k) or an array of length k.

Returns:

None

classmethod load_agent_model(file_name='single_prediction_collapsed_agent_model', folder='./saved_models/')[source]

Load a saved single-prediction collapsed agent model.

The configuration is loaded with joblib and the PyMC model is reconstructed by re-running __init__. The trace and prior samples are loaded from their NetCDF files if present.

Parameters:

  • file_name (str) – Base filename without extension. Expects to find {file_name}.joblib and, optionally, {file_name}_trace.nc and {file_name}_prior_samples.nc.

  • folder (str) – Folder the model is saved in.

Returns:

The loaded agent model.

Return type:

SinglePredictionCollapsedAgentModel

posterior_negative_sign_probability()[source]

Return the posterior probability that N_E is negative.

posterior_parameter_summaries(rng=None)[source]

Compute mean, std, skewness, and kurtosis of the posterior samples for each population parameter, in the same key format as agent_model.AgentModel.posterior_parameter_summaries(), so that experiment drivers can use the two model classes interchangeably.

Sampled population parameters are summarized directly. N_E moments are Rao–Blackwellized over the exact conditional sign probabilities. alpha_mu_A, alpha_mu_Y, N_b, and N_d are summarized from their coherent conditional reconstruction, so the returned moments describe the same posterior as an explicit model.

Parameters:

rng – Seed or initialized generator for the coefficient reconstruction (reused if draws are already cached).

Returns:

param_<name>_<moment> (scalar or k = 1) or param_<name>_<dim>_<moment> (k > 1) entries.

Return type:

dict

sample(X_o, pred_o, draws=1000, tune=1000, target_accept=0.85, chains=4, max_treedepth=15, init='jitter+adapt_diag', rng=None)[source]

Sample from the posterior given observed data. Stores the latest trace in self.

Parameters:

  • X_o (np.ndarray) – Observed feature vector of length k.

  • pred_o (float) – Observed scalar prediction for X_o.

  • draws (int) – Size of sample to draw from the posterior.

  • tune (int) – Number of tuning (warmup) iterations.

  • target_accept (float) – Target acceptance probability for NUTS.

  • chains (int) – Number of chains to sample.

  • max_treedepth (int) – Maximum tree depth for NUTS.

  • init (str) – Initialization method passed to pm.sample.

  • rng – Seed or initialized random number generator for reproducibility.

Returns:

None

sample_posterior_predictive(rng=None)[source]

This method generates a sample from the agent’s posterior beliefs. Using the trace stored in self, it reconstructs the marginalized coefficient vectors from their conditional Gaussian for each posterior draw, replaces the parameter values in the internal predictive SCM, and draws a posterior predictive sample from it.

Parameters:

rng – Seed or initialized random number generator for reproducibility.

Returns:

One (X, A, Y, mu_Y_cond, std_Y_cond) sample per draw.

Return type:

list

sample_posterior_predictive_CATE(A1_treatment, A0_treatment)[source]

This method returns a sample from the posterior CATE-distribution, and its sample mean and standard deviation. Under the collapsed model the CATE depends only on N_E, so it is the posterior draws of N_E multiplied by A1_treatment - A0_treatment.

Parameters:

  • A1_treatment (float) – Dosage value of higher dose treatment.

  • A0_treatment (float) – Dosage value of lower dose treatment.

Returns:

(CATE_samples, CATE_mean, CATE_std).

Return type:

tuple

sample_prior_predictive(draws=1000, rng=None)[source]

Method for sampling from the distribution based on the agent’s prior beliefs. For every draw of the predictive parameters from the prior, the marginalized coefficient vectors are drawn from their priors, the internal predictive SCM is updated, and one (X, A, Y) sample is generated from it.

Parameters:

  • draws (int) – Size of sample to draw.

  • rng – Seed or initialized random number generator for reproducibility.

Returns:

One [X, A, Y] triple per draw.

Return type:

list

sample_prior_predictive_CATE(A1_treatment, A0_treatment, draws=1000, rng=None)[source]

This method returns a sample from the prior CATE-distribution, and its sample mean and standard deviation. Under the collapsed model the CATE depends only on N_E, so it is obtained from the prior draws of N_E multiplied by A1_treatment - A0_treatment. It does not require conditioning on X. The prior draws are shared with the other prior predictive methods.

Parameters:

  • A1_treatment (float) – Dosage value of higher dose treatment.

  • A0_treatment (float) – Dosage value of lower dose treatment.

  • draws (int) – Size of sample to draw if prior samples are drawn here.

  • rng – Seed or initialized random number generator for reproducibility.

Returns:

(CATE_samples, CATE_mean, CATE_std).

Return type:

tuple

save_agent_model(file_name='single_prediction_collapsed_agent_model', folder='./saved_models/')[source]

Save the agent model configuration and available samples.

The trace and prior samples are written separately with ArviZ (NetCDF), and the rest of the configuration is pickled with joblib. The PyMC model, trace, and prior samples are temporarily detached before pickling and restored afterwards.

Parameters:

  • file_name (str) – Base filename without extension. Creates {file_name}.joblib and, when available, {file_name}_trace.nc and {file_name}_prior_samples.nc.

  • folder (str) – Folder to save the model into.

trace_diagnostics()[source]

Return basic sampler diagnostics for the current posterior trace.

Diagnostics cover the variables explored directly by NUTS and the deterministic quantities that drive the CATE and reduced likelihood. A deterministic component that is exactly constant is omitted because its R-hat and ESS are undefined but it has no Monte Carlo error.

Returns:

max_rhat, min_ess_bulk, min_ess_tail (computed with ArviZ), and n_divergences.

Return type:

dict
